config_method_reads: Put your %1$s link or a subscription link in the field, or click the button beside it to take it from the clipboard.
config_paste_body: Click Paste and Vazie VPN will read what is on your clipboard. It reads it here, on this Mac, and it goes nowhere else. A subscription link is the one exception: it is opened, to download its list.
mac_admin_prompt: Vazie VPN opens the tunnel for the whole Mac. It needs your password once for each connection.
mac_app_icon_body: Changes the icon in your Dock and in the menu bar. Your configurations and any live connection are untouched.
mac_build_signature: Vazie VPN for Mac %1$s (%2$s) · by Vazovsky
mac_check_note: Each site is asked twice: through the tunnel's own proxy, and the way any program does, following the system's settings. If the first works and the second does not, something else on this Mac is in the way.
mac_check_via_system: The way programs on this Mac ask
mac_engine_needed_body: The Xray engine is not on this Mac yet. It is downloaded once from its own release and checked against a pinned SHA-256.
mac_engine_pinned: Xray %1$s, checked against a pinned SHA-256 before it is ever run.
mac_engine_why: The engine is Xray, the program that speaks to your server. Vazie VPN starts it when you connect and stops it when you disconnect. It runs on this Mac only and listens on the loopback address, which nothing outside the Mac can reach.
mac_failure_admin_denied: The password wasn't entered, so the tunnel for the whole Mac wasn't opened
mac_failure_dns: The Mac's DNS couldn't be pointed at the tunnel. The tunnel was closed and nothing was changed
mac_failure_engine: The Xray engine isn't installed yet
mac_failure_integrity: The engine didn't pass Vazie VPN's check, so the tunnel for the whole Mac wasn't opened. Nothing was changed
mac_failure_kill_switch: The Kill Switch couldn't be turned on, so the tunnel wasn't opened without it. Nothing was changed
mac_failure_network: The Mac's connection changed while the tunnel was opening. Try again
mac_failure_proxy_taken: Another VPN or proxy app controls this Mac's network settings, so Vazie VPN can't route it. Turn the other one off and try again
mac_failure_proxy_taken_named: %1$s is connected and controls this Mac's network settings, so Vazie VPN can't route it. Disconnect it and try again
mac_failure_routes: The routes into the tunnel couldn't be set up. The tunnel was closed and nothing was changed
mac_failure_system_proxy: macOS wouldn't let Vazie VPN change the network settings
mac_failure_tun: The tunnel interface couldn't be opened
mac_failure_tun_bypassed: The tunnel opened, but the Mac's traffic doesn't go through it. The tunnel was closed and nothing was changed
mac_guidance_appearance_body: The theme and the icon: how Vazie VPN looks inside, in the Dock and in the menu bar.
mac_guidance_bug_body: Tell us in a short form: what happened and on which Mac. Every report is read.
mac_guidance_delete_body: Point at a row and press the bin, or right-click it. Deleting always asks first.
mac_guidance_guides_body: The menu bar, the Dock menu, the system proxy and notifications — how to use each.
mac_guidance_split_body: Choose sites that go around the VPN, or the only sites that go through it.
mac_guide_dock_body: Right-clicking the Vazie VPN icon in the Dock offers your recent configurations directly, and Connect or Disconnect. Nothing to set up — they are already there.
mac_guide_dock_step_1: Right-click (or Control-click) the Vazie VPN icon in the Dock.
mac_guide_dock_summary: Right-click the icon and pick one — nothing to set up.
mac_guide_dock_title: Your configurations under the Dock icon
mac_guide_engine_summary: The program that runs the tunnel.
mac_guide_menu_bar_body: The icon in the menu bar shows whether you are protected: a filled dot means connected. Click it for a small panel with the Connect button and your recent configurations — Android's widgets and Quick Settings tile, in one place.
mac_guide_menu_bar_step_1: Look for the Vazie VPN icon at the right end of the menu bar.
mac_guide_menu_bar_step_2: Click it to connect, disconnect or choose another configuration.
mac_guide_menu_bar_step_3: If the icon is hidden, drag it out with Command held down, or make room in System Settings → Control Center.
mac_guide_menu_bar_summary: State at a glance, and one click to connect.
mac_guide_menu_bar_title: Vazie VPN in the menu bar
mac_guide_notification_body_off: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can show a notification with a Disconnect button, so you can stop it from anywhere. Notifications are off right now, so it can't.
mac_guide_notification_body_on: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN shows a notification with a Disconnect button, so you can stop it from anywhere.
mac_guide_notification_step_1: Press Allow notifications above and accept macOS's question.
mac_guide_notification_step_2: If you declined earlier, open System Settings → Notifications → Vazie VPN.
mac_guide_notification_step_3: Choose Banners or Alerts; Alerts stay until you act on them.
mac_guide_notification_summary: A notification while the tunnel is up, with a Disconnect button.
mac_guide_system_proxy_body: Vazie VPN has two ways to reach your Mac. Whole Mac opens a tunnel interface that every program uses; it needs your password each time you connect. System proxy points the Mac's network settings at the engine, and puts them back as they were when you disconnect: browsers and most apps follow those settings, a few programs (command-line tools, some games) do not.
mac_guide_system_proxy_step_1: Connect. System Settings → Network shows the proxy while you are connected.
mac_guide_system_proxy_step_2: A program that ignores the system proxy needs its own setting: HTTP proxy 127.0.0.1 on the port shown there.
mac_guide_system_proxy_step_3: If Vazie VPN quits unexpectedly, the next launch puts the settings back.
mac_guide_system_proxy_summary: The system proxy, and what follows it.
mac_guide_system_proxy_title: How the tunnel reaches your Mac
mac_kill_switch_note: The block holds while Vazie VPN is running. If you quit or force-quit it, or restart the Mac, the block is lifted so you are never left without internet. It does not cover the moments before you connect. A change applies from the next connection
mac_kill_switch_proxy_mode: Switch to Whole Mac mode to use the Kill Switch
mac_kill_switch_row_body: If the VPN drops, block the internet instead of letting traffic out directly. Whole Mac mode only
mac_login_failed: macOS wouldn't change the login item.
mac_login_needs_approval: macOS needs your approval: System Settings → General → Login Items.
mac_login_row_body: Vazie VPN starts with your Mac and waits in the menu bar.
mac_login_unavailable: This copy of Vazie VPN can't be a login item; move it to Applications and open it from there.
mac_lost_blocked: Nothing is leaving this Mac, so nothing leaks. Reconnect, or Disconnect to get the internet back
mac_lost_open: Your traffic is going out directly, not through the VPN. Reconnect to protect it
mac_manage_list_body: Click a configuration to use it. Point at it to delete it, or right-click it — deleting always asks first.
mac_mode_note: The mode applies at the next connection.
mac_mode_proxy_body: Programs that follow the system proxy — browsers and most apps — go through the tunnel. No password.
mac_mode_title: How the tunnel reaches your Mac
mac_mode_whole_body: Every program goes through the tunnel, whether or not it follows the system proxy. Beta: it has not been proven on every Mac yet; if it does not hold, the app puts everything back and says so. Asks for your password each time you connect. Another VPN must be disconnected.
mac_notification_prompt_body: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can show a notification with a Disconnect button — so you can stop it from anywhere. Vazie VPN connects either way.
mac_onboarding_own_body: Vazie VPN ships with no servers, so the first thing to do is paste a VLESS link you already have. It is stored encrypted on this Mac and never uploaded — not to us, not to anyone. There is no account to create and nothing to pay for.
mac_onboarding_reach_body: An icon in the menu bar that shows the state at a glance, your configurations in the Dock menu, and a keyboard shortcut. Nothing to set up right now — I'll point out the basics in a moment.
mac_onboarding_welcome_body: I look after the tunnel in this app. I'll be on the home screen telling you whether you're protected, and I'll be sleeping when you're not. Give me thirty seconds and I'll show you around.
mac_onboarding_what_body: A VPN client: it opens an encrypted tunnel between this Mac and a server, so the network you are on sees traffic to that server and nothing about where it goes next. Vazie VPN is the client. It is not a service that watches over you.
mac_other_vpn_banner: %1$s is connected. A VPN like that can override the network settings Vazie VPN uses; if the connection does not hold, disconnect it first (System Settings → VPN).
mac_privacy_engine_download: The engine (Xray) comes inside the app, or is downloaded once from its own GitHub release; either way it is refused unless its SHA-256 matches the one pinned in Vazie VPN.
mac_privacy_engine_local: The engine runs on this Mac only and opens proxies that listen on 127.0.0.1 and nowhere else, on new ports for every connection. The configuration reaches it through a pipe, never through a file.
mac_privacy_export_body: Export produces the original share link, and that link contains the credentials that connect to the server. Anyone who receives it can use the server as you. Vazie VPN copies it to the clipboard at the moment you ask and clears the clipboard 30 seconds later.
mac_privacy_logs_body: Vazie VPN never writes a key, a UUID, a share link or a server address into any log, and starts the engine with logging off.
mac_privacy_stores_configs: Your configurations: the server address, the port, the transport and security settings, and the keys needed to connect.
mac_privacy_surfaces_menu: The Dock menu offers up to three configurations by name. A name that looks like an address, a link, an e-mail, an IP or a UUID is left out rather than shortened.
mac_privacy_surfaces_network: The one site Vazie VPN always talks to is the Vazie backend, for the About links and the questions. A subscription's server is asked once, when you add that subscription; and the engine's release page, once, if you download the engine.
mac_privacy_surfaces_notification: The notification, if you allow it, shows the connection state and nothing else. It never names a configuration.
mac_privacy_surfaces_title: The menu bar, the Dock and notifications
mac_privacy_system_body: To send apps through the tunnel, Vazie VPN changes the proxy settings of your Wi-Fi and Ethernet services while you are connected — and only those.
mac_privacy_system_restore: What the settings said before is kept in a small file and put back when you disconnect or quit. If the app is ever killed, the next launch puts them back.
mac_privacy_vpn_body: While connected, the traffic of the apps that follow the system proxy goes through the server in the configuration you chose. That server can see the destinations they ask for, exactly as your network provider could otherwise. Vazie VPN is the client; it does not run in between. Programs that ignore the system proxy are not tunnelled.
mac_privacy_vpn_dns: Names are looked up by the server, not by your provider, for everything that goes through the tunnel.
mac_privacy_where_encrypted: Configurations and their keys are encrypted on this Mac with a key held in your Keychain. Other apps cannot read the file, and it is never part of any backup you do not make yourself.
mac_privacy_where_plain: Your theme, icon, sites for split tunneling and dismissed tips are in a plain file — they are preferences, not secrets, and keeping them apart means a display setting cannot break the store that holds your keys.
mac_privacy_where_sync: Nothing is synced. Vazie VPN does not use iCloud, so your configurations never travel through your Apple account.
mac_reconnect_row_body: Brings the connection back after a dropped network, sleep or a server that stopped answering. It gives up after a few tries
mac_recovery_banner_blocking: A previous session ended unexpectedly while the Kill Switch was on, so the internet may be blocked. Restore the network
mac_recovery_banner_settings: A previous session ended unexpectedly, and the Mac's DNS or IPv6 may still be set for the tunnel. Put them back as they were
mac_recovery_banner_supervisor: A previous session ended unexpectedly. Restore the network to be sure nothing is left changed
mac_recovery_failed: The network couldn't be restored. Try again, or restart the Mac
mac_recovery_prompt: Vazie VPN puts the Mac's network back as it was. It needs your password once.
mac_split_mode_exclude_body: The sites you pick go straight through your provider; everything else uses the VPN.
mac_split_mode_include_body: Only the sites you pick use the VPN; everything else goes straight through your provider.
mac_split_mode_off_body: Everything that follows the Mac's network settings uses the tunnel.
mac_split_note: A Mac routes by name, not by program, so this list holds sites. A site also covers its subdomains. Addresses on your own network (localhost, 192.168.x.x, .local) never go through the tunnel. Changes apply at once.
mac_split_note_whole: The list is applied the next time you connect (the Mac's engine reads it then).
mac_subtitle_reconnecting: The connection dropped. Vazie VPN is bringing it back
mac_tour_done_body: Vazie VPN also lives in the menu bar and under its Dock icon. None of it is required — the guides are there when you want them.
mac_uninstall_body: The tunnel is closed, your Mac's network settings are put back, and the app is moved to the Trash with its preferences and the engine it downloaded. Your configurations and their key stay on this Mac, so installing again finds them.
mac_uninstall_delete_configs: Also delete my configurations (cannot be undone)
mac_uninstall_list: Nothing of the browser extension's helper is touched.
mac_uninstall_row_body: The app and everything it keeps on this Mac.
tour_configuration_body: Your configurations are here — everything Vazie VPN connects through. Click a row to choose it, or “+ Add” to add one.
tour_settings_body: The gear opens Settings, with the guides for the menu bar, the Dock and everything else.
